name: Shahroud Data Center Township
developer: Semnan Science and Technology Park / local public-private partners
notes: Mehr reported an MoU signed in Shahroud for what was described as Iran's largest data-center township, with more than 4,000 billion tomans investment and 30,000 sq m of land; power/capacity not disclosed.

name: Pishgaman Tosee Ertebatat Yazd Data Center
notes: Opening report says the Yazd data center provides colocation, cloud, security, wireless/fiber connectivity, dark fiber to the national internet hub, redundant UPS and generator backup; power described as a 900A three-phase dedicated substation.

name: Isatis Data Center
notes: Operator site lists Isatis Datacenter in Yazd at Shahid Motahari Street, Eqbal Technology Center units C20/C22/C25, offering virtual machines, colocation, dedicated servers and shared hosting.

name: Saba Foulad Khalij Fars Data Center
notes: Local report/interview with Saba Foulad's ICT manager says the company launched an equipped Data Center in the northern site of the Persian Gulf Special Economic Zone, serving factory connectivity and IT services in Tehran and Hormozgan; publication page lacked a clear article date, so checked date used.

name: Asiatech Milad Tower Data Center
notes: DCD reported Asiatech opened a 700 sq m colocation/networking data center in Milad Tower, western Tehran, with space for several thousand customers; capacity in MW not disclosed.

name: Pars Online Data Center - Tehran
notes: Datacenter directory listings place Pars Online's Tehran facility at/near Green Jewel Building and describe N+1 redundancy, colocation, dedicated/managed servers, IaaS/cloud and two large-scale sites with thousands of physical servers; directory evidence, not primary.

name: AFRANET Data Center
notes: Data center directories list Afranet DC in Tehran, including a No. 12 Hoveyeze/Sahand Street address and colocation category; no capacity disclosed.

name: Fanap / ArvanCloud Pardis IT Town National Network Data Center
notes: Iran International, citing sources, reported a Huawei-based national network/data-center project in final stages under ArvanCloud management beneath Fanap's administrative building in Pardis IT Town, about 20 km northeast of Tehran, with about 400 server racks; unconfirmed by operator/government, so grade C.

name: IRIB Ardabil Central Data Center Building
developer: Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) / Ardabil provincial center
notes: IRIB News reported groundbreaking for the first central data-center building at the Ardabil broadcast center to support infrastructure, storage and backing of internet/virtual media; no capacity disclosed.

name: Amin Internet Data Center
notes: Operator website lists Amin Data Center in Qom, Amin Boulevard near Alley 51, offering cloud infrastructure, server hosting, GPU/dedicated/virtual servers and rack colocation services.

name: Noor Data Center
notes: Operator website describes Noor Data Center services including rack rental, VPS and hosting, and states Qom-based organizations can connect to the center via wireless or fiber; capacity not disclosed.

name: Qazvin Provincial Data Center
developer: Iran Ministry of ICT / Iran IT Organization / Qazvin Province
notes: Iran's Ministry of ICT quoted the Qazvin provincial ICT director saying a data center would be built in the province in coordination with the Iran IT Organization to secure data for public-service agencies and online businesses; capacity not disclosed.

name: Gorgan Municipality Data Center
notes: Mehr's report on Gorgan 1404 program quotes the secretariat head saying data centralization and launch of a municipal data center had been completed as electronic-city infrastructure; older municipal/internal facility evidence, no capacity disclosed.

name: Birjand Data Processing IT Complex Data Center Upgrade
developer: Mojtame Fanavari Etelaat Dade Pardaz Birjand
notes: Etarh project page describes a feasibility/business plan for upgrading a data center and specialized network lab for Mojtame Fanavari Etelaat Dade Pardaz Birjand in Birjand, South Khorasan, with fixed investment of 40,045,000 thousand rials and working capital of 3,705,031 thousand rials; status inferred as planned from feasibility-plan wording.
